en.name: Innocent III
en.summary: One of the most powerful medieval popes, who gave verbal approval to Francis of Assisi's new religious movement.
en.body: Elected at just thirty-seven, Innocent III presided over the medieval papacy at the height of its political and spiritual authority, intervening in the affairs of kings across Europe. He convened the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215, one of the most consequential councils of the Middle Ages, which issued sweeping reforms of Church discipline and doctrine. Despite initial hesitation, he gave verbal approval around 1209-1210 to the way of life proposed by a young man named Francis of Assisi, permitting the movement that would become the Franciscan order to begin.
